angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 744,399 km at 156.81 pc = 0.06 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 6.3771 +/- 0.0240 mas (same row, RUWE 0.99): 156.81 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.07 +/- 0.01 solar radii from Jordán et al. 2019, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-287 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....157..100J/abstract): 744,399 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.056 +/- 0.022 solar masses from Jordán et al. 2019, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-287 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....157..100J/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5695 +/- 58 K from Jordán et al. 2019, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-287 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....157..100J/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Jordán et al. 2019, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-287 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....157..100J/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-287.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.403, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
